prerequisites: Basic behavior of physics and electronics

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the methodology to analyze measuring systems.
Learn how to understand technical papers.
Learn how to read the data sheet of the most popular electronic instruments.
Apply knowledge to understand the operating principle of the most popular electronic instruments.
Express concepts learnt during the course with the appropriate language.
Learn the theoretical and methodological tools to independently carry on his/her own updates.
Gain basic preparation concerning the measurement methods and electronic instrumentation.
Acquire knowledge on Labview and concretely experiment theoretical aspects.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of measurement science: basis of statistics, statistical analysis of the results of repeated tests and evaluation of the measurement uncertainty, uncertainty propagation (2 CFU)
Electrical measurements and related methods, devices, and calculations to measure DC and AC voltages, current, and resistance. (1 CFU)
Analysis of signals in the time domain: oscilloscope. Operating principle, time base, channel y, channel x (1 CFU)
Analysis of signals in the frequency domain: spectrum analyzer. Operating principle, application, performance (1 CFU)
A/D converters, digital multimeter, PC-based acquisition systems and signal processing Counter/frequency meter (1 CFU)
LABORATORY: Experiences aimed at measuring basic electrical quantities (3 CFU)

assessment_methods.method: Mandatory written test (solving practical problems and multiple-choice questions)

assessment_rules: The exam consists of a mandatory written test and an optional oral test. The written test includes two problem-solving questions (11 points each) and five multiple-choice questions (2 points for correct, 0 for no answer, -1 for wrong). A score of at least 18/30 on the written test is required to access the optional oral part, which can add -2/30 to +2/30 to the score. A mandatory laboratory activity requires reports, which are graded and contribute 20% to the final grade. The final grade is calculated as 0.8 * (overall exam score) + 0.2 * (laboratory score).
